sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:108955
Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 18600 of 2023

Applicant :- Ajay Kumar
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Akhilesh Kumar Dwivedi

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Akhilesh Kumar Dwivedi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Amit Kumar Shukla,
learned brief holder for the State-respondent.
2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in PST No. 20 of 2018 (State Vs. Ajay Kumar) arising out of Case Crime No. 361 of 2017, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and 4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Jalesar, District- Etah, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. From the perusal of the record, it appears that applicant was earlier released on bail but thereafter he absconded and when coercive measures were taken against him then he appeared before the court concerned.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant was earlier released on bail in the present matter and he continuously attended the trial court but due to his livelihood in the month of November, 2022, he had to go to Delhi, therefore, he could not appear before the trial court and when he came to know that coercive measures are being taken against him then he himself Ajay Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3704359/
1 surrendered before the court concerned on 23.3.2023 and filed recall application to recall the NBW issued against him but his recall application was dismissed and when he filed bail application then his bail application was also rejected.

sentences.text:
5. He further submitted that applicant was not having any intention to abscond and in near future,
he is ready to appear on each and every dates, either in person or through his counsel, therefore,
considering the facts and circumstances of the case, applicant may be released on bail.
6.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant, at the stage of final hearing, absconded and when process under Section 82 & 83 Cr.P.C. was issued then he appeared, therefore, it appears that he intentionally abstained from the proceeding of the Court and if he is released on bail then he will again abscond, therefore, he should not be released on bail.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. From the perusal of the record, it appears that when the case was posted for final hearing in the month of November, 2022 then applicant absconded and he did not turn up after November, 2022 and NBW was issued against him and thereafter process under Section 82 & 83 Cr.P.C. was also issued and only thereafter he appeared on 23.3.2023 i.e. after about four months.
9.

As from the perusal of the rejection order, it appears that trial of the case is at its last leg and dates are being fixed for final hearing and till date trial could not be concluded due to non co-operation of the applicant, therefore, in my view applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, the instant bail is rejected.

11. However, as from the rejection order, it reflects that dates are being fixed for final hearing,
therefore, it appears that trial is at its last leg, therefore, trial court is directed to conclude the trial of the case within two months from the date of production of the certified copy of the order passed today.
12. Registrar(compliance) of this Court is directed to communicate the order passed by this Court to the trial court for compliance within 48 hours.

13. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 18.5.2023 KK Patel
Ajay Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 May, 2023
